summary:
Project Azdi (SpaceFire SI) is an interactive, Super Intelligence-assisted fire safety dashboard and audited machine learning pipeline built on seven NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion datasets: FLEX (PSI-69), FLEX-2 (PSI-68), BASS (PSI-26), BASS-II (PSI-25), and SAFFIRE I, II, and III (PSI-98, PSI-99, PSI-100).

To ensure scientific rigor for Moon and Mars spacecraft design, we audited and unified 545 experimental records with strict data provenance tags (338 verified real measurements, 199 astronaut log entries with manual nitrogen or fan intervention, and 8 test-matrix range summaries excluded from modeling). Our platform delivers five defensible modules: (1) an Audited Data Explorer and Material Safety Leaderboard with a transparent Engineering Fire Risk Formula, (2) a GroupKFold-validated FLEX Droplet ML Simulator (ROC-AUC 0.793), (3) an empirical Solid Flammability Boundary Map (O2 vs. airflow), (4) calibrated SAFFIRE camera telemetry curves across 280,000+ frames, and (5) a RAG Advisor citing verbatim ISS astronaut logs.
details:
1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Project Azdi (SpaceFire SI) transforms decades of complex NASA microgravity combustion archives (PSI-25, PSI-26, PSI-68, PSI-69, PSI-98, PSI-99, PSI-100) into an interactive 5-module decision-support dashboard and reproducible Python ML pipeline:

• Module 1 — Audited Data Explorer & Material Leaderboard: Unifies 545 records with explicit data_origin provenance ("real", "parsed_from_text", "synthetic"). Excludes synthetic test-matrix rows and unverified crew-intervened runs from safety rankings, evaluating 336 verified real runs alongside an explicit, transparent Engineering Fire Risk Index formula.

• Module 2 — FLEX Liquid Droplet ML Simulator: Trained on 262 real droplet combustion tests in the ISS CIR chamber (PSI-69). Predicts radiative self-extinguishment vs. micro-explosion (Disruption) or full burnout, extinction diameter (d_ext, R2 = 0.662), and burning rate constant K, while warning engineers when extinguished n-heptane droplets transition into invisible "cool flames" (~500-800 K).

• Module 3 — Solid Material Flammability Boundary Map (O2 vs. Airflow): Maps 62 strictly verified solid polymer and fabric burns from NASA/TM-20210011385 (Tables 5.1 and 7.1) and SAFFIRE-I/II. Visualizes the low-velocity radiative quenching zone (2.2-5.0 cm/s), the hazardous ventilation window (5-30 cm/s), high-velocity blow-off (47 cm/s), and why Earth 1-g upward screening (NASA-STD-6001) fails on silicone and opposed-flow fabrics.

• Module 4 — Calibrated SAFFIRE Camera Telemetry Curves: Processes 280,000+ C1/C2 camera JPEG frames from SAFFIRE I, II, and III into 1,344 calibrated 5-second time-series bins. Uses per-camera median filtering to reject periodic LED strobe flashes, masks pre/post-test floodlights in SAFFIRE-II, and subtracts pre-ignition dark baselines—matching official NASA CSV burn times (420.0s Concurrent and 70.0s Opposed in SAFFIRE-I; 0.0s on self-extinguished Silicone).

• Module 5 — Verbatim RAG Fire Safety Advisor: Grounds every engineering recommendation in verbatim quotes from ISS astronaut logs (Don Pettit, Reid Wiseman, Alexander Gerst) and NASA technical reports—such as why directed N2 jets in BASS Test #3 entrained oxygen into the wake flame instead of extinguishing it.

2. BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

As NASA prepares for Artemis lunar habitats and Mars transit missions, spacecraft fire safety engineers must select cabin materials, atmosphere compositions (such as Exploration Atmosphere 8.2 psia / 34% O2), and ventilation emergency protocols. Project Azdi prevents dangerous misinterpretations of raw archival data (such as confusing manual astronaut nitrogen shutoffs with material self-extinguishment) and gives mission designers an instant, scientifically defensible tool to test material and ventilation trade-offs.

3. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE

• Data Unification, Telemetry Calibration & ML Pipeline: Python 3, NumPy, Pandas, OpenPyXL (implemented in spacefire_ml_pipeline.py with custom GroupKFold validation, Gradient Boosted Regressors, and Random Forest Classifiers).

• Interactive Front-End Dashboard: Standalone HTML5, JavaScript (ES6), Tailwind CSS, and Chart.js (spacefire_si_dashboard.html, requiring zero server setup).

4. CREATIVITY & FACTORS CONSIDERED

Rather than treating all dataset rows as a black-box ML problem, we performed a rigorous physical and methodological audit:

• Eliminated Group Data Leakage: Replaced naive random cross-validation with GroupKFold grouped by experimental series and material geometry.

• Separated Physics by Fuel Phase: Decoupled quiescent liquid droplets (FLEX) from forced-convection solid materials (BASS/SAFFIRE).

• Solved Optical Strobe & Floodlight Artifacts: Built a custom median-entropy baseline subtraction algorithm to extract true flame durations from raw SAFFIRE JPEG telemetry.

5. ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) USE

Super Intelligence (Google Gemini) was utilized to assist with Python code generation for parsing multi-archive NASA PSI datasets, implementing GroupKFold validation and telemetry calibration scripts, structuring the interactive HTML/Chart.js dashboard, and formatting documentation. All experimental data, physical constants (13.1 kJ/g O2 calorimetry), and verbatim quotes originate strictly from official NASA PSI datasets and technical reports. No NASA logos or branding elements were generated or modified.
